issues.description: The method Milkable.messageOnMilk() has conflicting return-type information across the problem statement and the reference implementation. In the problem statement the Milkable interface is declared as messageOnMilk(): boolean (problem_statement.md lines 51-53) and the textual Part 2 instructions state "messageOnMilk() should return true if milking was successful, false otherwise" (problem_statement.md lines 92-94). However, the PlantUML in the same problem statement shows Seal.messageOnMilk():String (problem_statement.md line 33) and Goat.messageOnMilk():String (problem_statement.md line 44), and the solution repository defines Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning String (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5) with Seal and Goat implementations returning String (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java line 19, solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java line 15). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement messageOnMilk() as boolean or String and will cause compile-time or behavioral mismatches depending on which interpretation they follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Pick a single return type for Milkable.messageOnMilk() and make all artifacts consistent. Preferred quick resolution: update the problem statement UML and textual Part 2 instructions to specify that messageOnMilk() returns a String (e.g., "Seal <name> is milked") to match the provided solution and examples, and clarify example outputs. Alternatively, if the intended behavior is boolean, change the solution's Milkable interface and all Seal/Goat implementations to return boolean and update the sample outputs, tests, and the UML accordingly. Ensure template files and tests (if any) are aligned with the chosen type.
